issues.description: Check filename and CheckID say 'single' but logic and PR title detect 'multiple' — mismatched naming will mislead future readers.
issues.detail: The directory, class, and CheckID are 'compute_instance_single_network_interface' while the PR is titled 'detect VMs with multiple network interfaces' and the FAIL path triggers on multiple NICs. A check named for its passing condition reads backwards; a future reader auditing failures will hunt for a 'multiple' check that does not exist. Pick one frame and apply it everywhere.

issues.description: GKE detection by 'gke-' name prefix is an undocumented, brittle heuristic with no stated invariant.
issues.detail: The branch `instance.name.startswith('gke-')` carries the entire MANUAL-vs-FAIL decision, yet nowhere is the invariant 'GKE-managed node VMs are exactly those whose name starts with gke-' stated or cited. Users can name any VM 'gke-foo' and silently escape FAIL; legitimate GKE node pools with custom prefixes get FAILed. Use the GKE label/metadata (`goog-gke-node`) or document the heuristic explicitly as a literate comment.

issues.description: The 'no network interfaces' branch silently reports PASS, which is asymptotically wrong for the check's intent.
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0`, status remains 'PASS' from initialization and status_extended says the instance has no NICs. A GCE instance with zero NICs is either impossible or a data-fetch bug; reporting PASS hides the anomaly. Either treat this as MANUAL/ERROR with an explicit comment, or state the invariant that zero NICs cannot occur and why PASS is acceptable.

issues.description: interface_names is computed unconditionally even when there are zero or one interfaces and the list is unused on most paths.
issues.detail: Minor, but `interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces]` runs for every instance and is only meaningfully consumed in the multi-NIC branches. Not a hot path — this is explicitly the kind of thing not worth optimizing — but it is worth a one-line literate comment noting the list is built eagerly for uniform message formatting. Mention only because the file otherwise lacks any complexity/intent commentary.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model drops accessConfigs/natIP data already being parsed two lines above — duplicated traversal without shared structure.
issues.detail: In `_get_instances`, the loop computes `public_ip` from `accessConfigs` and then constructs `NetworkInterface` objects that deliberately omit access config / IP information. Future checks (public IP per-NIC, IP forwarding per-NIC) will require re-parsing the same `networkInterfaces` blob. Carry access_configs (or at least a per-NIC public_ip bool) on the model now; the data structure choice is paying interest already.

issues.description: No test exercises the GKE MANUAL branch or the zero-interface edge case — claimed behavior is tested-correct only for the easy paths.
issues.detail: The docstring promises a MANUAL outcome for GKE-prefixed multi-NIC instances, but the visible tests cover only single, two, and three-NIC non-GKE instances plus the empty-list case. The most behaviorally interesting branch ('gke-' prefix → MANUAL) appears unverified in the provided diff. Add a test asserting MANUAL for a `gke-foo` instance with 2+ NICs, and one for `interface_count == 0`.

review.summary: UNDER-AUDITED with a NEEDS-LITERATE-COMMENT flavor. The algorithm itself is trivial (count NICs per instance, O(N) over instances, O(M) over NICs — total O(sum of NICs), entirely appropriate), so complexity is not the issue. The issues are naming (the artifact is named for the passing condition while the PR sells the failing condition), an undocumented GKE heuristic doing load-bearing classification on a string prefix, a silent PASS on zero NICs, a missed opportunity to model accessConfigs on NetworkInterface for downstream checks, and missing tests for exactly the branch the docstring most prominently advertises. None of this is a correctness emergency; all of it is the kind of thing a careful reader will trip on six months from now.
